properties.natural_language: All incoming TCP connection requests from mining clients must be validated before session establishment; the mining.hello message must contain a valid agent string, supported protocol version, host, and port.
The mining.hello request must specify a protocol version compatible with EthereumStratum/2.0.0; incompatible versions must be rejected with an appropriate error code.

Worker authorization credentials submitted via mining.authorize must be validated against the session's authorized worker list; unauthorized worker tokens must be rejected with a 3xx authentication error.
All JSON messages received on the Stratum TCP connection must be valid JSON terminated with a line feed (LF) character; malformed JSON must be rejected with a 4xx syntax error.
Hex values in Stratum protocol messages must be lowercase, without 0x prefix, and use minimal significant digits; non-conforming hex formats must be rejected.
For mining.submit requests, the worker token must correspond to an authorized worker in the current session; unauthorized tokens must result in a 3xx error.
The job ID in mining.submit must match an active job within the current session; submissions referencing invalid or expired job IDs must be rejected.
Mining configuration parameters received via mining.set (epoch, target, extranonce) must be validated; extranonce must not exceed 6 bytes.
Mining job notifications received via mining.notify must contain a valid job ID, block number, and header hash; the stale indicator must be honored when determining whether to continue mining.
Session resumption requests must include a previously valid session ID; the server must verify the session exists in cache before restoring state.
The session error counter must monotonically increase with each error; once it reaches the maxerrors threshold, the server must force-disconnect the client.
A mining session must always be in exactly one of the defined lifecycle states: TCP-connected, hello-exchanged, session-established, workers-authorized, mining-active, or terminated.
After a successful mining.subscribe, the server must return a unique session ID and the session must transition to the established state.
After session resumption with a valid cached session ID, the server must restore the extranonce and active jobs without requiring re-authorization of workers.
After session resumption fails (session expired/not found), the server must create a new session with a new ID, and the client must re-authorize workers.
After a valid solution submission, the server must respond with either acceptance or rejection; accepted submissions must credit the submitting worker.
If no activity occurs within the idle timeout period, the server must force-disconnect the client to free resources.
Compressed messages must only be accepted if gzip compression was negotiated during the hello exchange; otherwise they must be rejected with a 4xx error.
TCP message delivery must be in-order; out-of-order messages could cause protocol state desynchronization between miner and pool.
An attacker must not be able to impersonate a legitimate pool server without controlling the network path; MITM attacks must be prevented by the network layer.
Before executing SLOAD, the EVM must verify that remaining gas is at least 800 (the EIP-1884 repriced cost); insufficient gas must trigger an out-of-gas exception.
Before executing BALANCE or EXTCODEHASH, the EVM must verify that remaining gas is at least 700; insufficient gas must trigger an out-of-gas exception.
After successful gas deduction for a trie-accessing opcode, the remaining gas must be reduced by exactly the EIP-1884 specified amount and the trie access must proceed.
After executing SELFBALANCE (0x47), the contract's own balance must be pushed onto the stack with only 5 gas consumed (GasFastStep).
Contracts that perform SLOAD within the 2300 gas stipend of a transfer() or send() call will revert after EIP-1884, since SLOAD now costs 800 gas instead of 200.
ERC-165 supportsInterface callbacks using SLOAD may revert if the 30,000 gas stipend is insufficient given the repriced SLOAD cost of 800 gas.
The gas cost schedule must be updated atomically at fork activation; SLOAD=800, BALANCE=700, EXTCODEHASH=700 must be enforced consistently across all EVM implementations.
Solidity and other compilers must not generate code that depends on specific SLOAD/BALANCE gas costs; compiler-generated code patterns must remain functional after the repricing.
The block timestamp used in difficulty calculation must be within acceptable bounds relative to the parent block timestamp; timestamp manipulation must not be possible.
Uncle references in the parent block header must be cryptographically verifiable via the unclesHash; false uncle claims must be detectable.

After computing the difficulty adjustment factor, it must be bounded between -99 and the uncle factor (1 or 2); the formula max((uncle_factor) - ((timestamp - parent.timestamp) // 9), -99) must be applied correctly.
After computing child difficulty, the result must equal parent.difficulty + (parent.difficulty // 2048) * adjustment_factor.
The uncle factor must be set to 2 if the parent block contains uncle references, and 1 otherwise; this ensures difficulty accounts for total block production rate.
Manipulating the uncle rate must not increase effective issuance; the EIP-100 formula must neutralize uncle rate gaming strategies.
The target block time of approximately 15 seconds must be maintained; the 3% difficulty decrease accounts for the approximately 7% uncle rate.

For BALANCE, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODECOPY, and EXTCODEHASH opcodes, the target address must be checked against the access list before gas charging; cold access costs 2600 gas and warm access costs 100 gas.
External account data requests from executing smart contracts must validate the target address format before performing access list lookup.
After a cold account access, the address must be added to the warm access list so subsequent accesses in the same transaction are charged the lower warm rate.
After executing a stack-only environment opcode (ADDRESS, ORIGIN, CALLER, etc.), the correct context value must be pushed to the stack and GAS_BASE (2) must be charged.
After RETURNDATACOPY with offset + size exceeding returndatasize, the EVM must revert execution; valid bounds must result in successful copy to memory.
After BLOBHASH with an index >= len(blob_versioned_hashes), zero must be pushed to the stack; valid indices must return the correct versioned hash.
SELFBALANCE must always return the same value as BALANCE(ADDRESS) but at 5 gas instead of the access-list-dependent BALANCE cost.
EXTCODEHASH must return zero for empty accounts (balance=0, nonce=0, code=empty) and non-existent accounts; non-empty accounts must return keccak256 of bytecode.
Memory expansion gas for CALLDATACOPY, CODECOPY, and RETURNDATACOPY must be calculated based on destOffset + size; copy gas must be GAS_COPY * ceil(size / 32).
Return data buffer must be cleared/set correctly between CALLs and must not be accessible across transaction boundaries to prevent information leakage.
Non-existent accounts must not trigger different gas costs than empty accounts when queried; gas cost leakage could reveal account existence information.

Before accepting a transaction, the sender's CodeHash must be retrieved from state and compared against EMPTYCODEHASH (0xc5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470); transactions from addresses with deployed code must be rejected.
The EIP-3607 CodeHash check must occur after nonce verification; the ordering relative to other validation checks must be consistent across all client implementations.
All transactions in a received block must pass the EIP-3607 sender validation; blocks containing any transaction from a sender with deployed code must be rejected entirely.
After verifying the sender's CodeHash equals EMPTYCODEHASH, the transaction must proceed to further validation checks; the sender is confirmed as an EOA.
After detecting a sender with deployed code (CodeHash != EMPTYCODEHASH), the transaction must be rejected and must not be included in any block.
The address collision attack requiring ~2^80 operations (~$10B compute) must remain economically infeasible; EIP-3607 provides defense-in-depth against this attack vector.
There must be no legitimate use case for transactions originating from contract addresses; if future protocol changes introduce such use cases, EIP-3607 must be revised.
For eth_call and eth_estimateGas RPC requests, the EIP-3607 sender code check may be bypassed to allow simulation of transactions from contract addresses.
Incoming inclusion list messages on the gossipsub topic must have transaction data within MAX_BYTES_PER_INCLUSION_LIST (8192 bytes); oversized messages must be REJECTED with peer score penalty.
The slot in an inclusion list message must equal the current slot or the previous slot; messages with other slot values must be REJECTED.
The BLS signature on a SignedInclusionList must be cryptographically valid; invalid signatures must result in REJECT with peer score penalty.
The validator_index in an inclusion list message must be a member of the inclusion list committee for the specified slot; non-members must be REJECTED.
Each validator may submit at most 2 valid inclusion lists per slot; subsequent submissions must be IGNORED without peer penalty.
REJECT-level validation failures must penalize the sending peer's score; IGNORE-level failures must drop the message without penalizing the peer.
Network propagation must deliver inclusion lists before attestation due time; late-arriving lists are IGNORED, potentially reducing effective committee size.
After all validation checks pass, the inclusion list must be accepted locally and forwarded to gossip peers for propagation.
Responses to inclusion_list_by_committee_indices requests must return at most MAX_REQUEST_INCLUSION_LIST (16) SignedInclusionList objects matching the requested slot and committee indices.
The fork version hierarchy must be correctly configured; incorrect fork context could cause valid messages to be rejected or invalid messages accepted.
Block context values (coinbase, timestamp, number, PREVRANDAO, gaslimit, chainid) must be correctly set by the block producer and verified by consensus before EVM execution begins.

BLOCKHASH requests must verify the requested block number is within the valid range [current - 256, current - 1]; requests for future blocks, the current block, or blocks older than 256 must return zero.
After executing any block context opcode (COINBASE, TIMESTAMP, NUMBER, PREVRANDAO, GASLIMIT, CHAINID), the value must be pushed to stack, GAS_BASE (2) charged, and PC incremented by 1.
After BLOCKHASH with a valid in-range block number, the correct 32-byte block hash must be pushed to the stack with 20 gas (GAS_BLOCK_HASH) charged.
PREVRANDAO must return the randao_mix from the parent beacon block; validators must not be able to predict or manipulate this value beyond their own influence on randao reveals.
TIMESTAMP must be monotonically increasing; non-monotonic timestamps could break time-dependent contract logic.
CHAIN_ID must be immutable and correctly identify the network; chain ID manipulation could enable replay attacks across networks.
Block hashes for the most recent 256 blocks must always be available in state; missing data must not cause BLOCKHASH to return incorrect zero values for valid block numbers.
Stack overflow must be checked before pushing block context values; if the stack already has 1024 elements, a StackOverflowError must be raised.
After executing a binary bitwise operation (AND, OR, XOR), the result must be the correct bitwise combination of the two 256-bit operands, pushed to the stack with 3 gas (GAS_VERY_LOW) charged.
After executing BYTE(i, x) with i < 32, the result must be the byte at position i (big-endian, 0 = most significant); for i >= 32, the result must be 0.
After SHL/SHR with shift >= 256, the result must be 0; after SAR with shift >= 256, the result must be 0 for positive values or MAX_VALUE (2^256-1) for negative values.
After SHL with shift < 256, the result must be (value << shift) masked to 256 bits (MAX_VALUE = 2^256 - 1).
All bitwise operations (AND, OR, XOR, NOT, BYTE, SHL, SHR, SAR) must consume exactly GAS_VERY_LOW (3 gas); insufficient gas must trigger an out-of-gas exception.
All bitwise operations must be constant-time for same input sizes; variable-time operations could leak information through timing analysis.
Stack underflow must be detected before popping operands for any bitwise operation; binary operations require 2 elements, NOT requires 1.

After PUSH0, zero must be pushed to stack with GAS_BASE (2) charged; after PUSH1-PUSH32, the N immediate bytes must be read from bytecode, converted to U256 big-endian, and pushed with GAS_VERY_LOW (3) charged.
After PUSH N, the program counter must be incremented by 1 + N (1 for the opcode, N for the immediate bytes).
After POP, the top stack element must be removed and discarded with GAS_BASE charged and PC incremented by 1.
After DUP N, the element at position N (0-indexed from top) must be duplicated to the stack top with GAS_VERY_LOW (3) charged.
After SWAP N, the top element and the element at position N must be exchanged with GAS_VERY_LOW (3) charged.
Before DUP or SWAP operations, the stack depth must be validated; item_number must be less than len(evm.stack) or a StackUnderflowError must be raised.
The stack depth must never exceed 1024 elements; PUSH and DUP operations that would exceed this limit must raise a StackOverflowError.
Bytecode must be immutable during execution; PUSH instructions reading from bytecode offsets must not be affected by concurrent modifications.
The program counter must only be modified through explicit control flow (JUMP, JUMPI) or normal instruction advancement; arbitrary PC manipulation must be prevented.
EVM trace requests must only be accepted when tracing is explicitly enabled via configuration; trace endpoints must not be available on production RPC nodes.

After each opcode execution, the trace JSON must contain pre-execution state (pc, op, gas, stack, memSize) and post-execution data (gasCost, returnData); the output must be a single JSON line per opcode.
After transaction execution completes, a summary JSON line must be emitted containing stateRoot, output, gasUsed, and pass/fail status.
When an error occurs on a non-STOP opcode, the trace must include an error field; errors on the STOP opcode must suppress trace output for that line.
Trace output must accurately reflect actual EVM execution; inaccurate traces could mask consensus bugs or security vulnerabilities.
All Ethereum clients must implement the trace format consistently; inconsistent implementations prevent effective cross-client differential fuzzing.
Trace execution is an expensive operation; it must be rate-limited and resource-bounded to prevent denial-of-service attacks against debug nodes.
